articles.title_zh: How the downfall of Serbia's Vučiċ mirrored that of Hungary's Orbán
facts_zh:
How the downfall of Serbia's Vučiċ mirrored that of Hungary's Orbán
- Published
When they met in northern Serbia last November, Serbian President Aleksandar Vučiċ and Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán could hardly have guessed they would both be out of power within a year.
Both were ousted by popular movements - Orbán fell first, in April, defeated by Péter Magyar's Tisza party.
Then last Sunday a student movement less than two years old won Serbia's parliamentary elections by a landslide.

articles.title_zh: Crypto firm Binance covers 90% of losses after $6.3bn hack
facts_zh:
Crypto firm Binance covers 90% of losses after $6.3bn hack
- Published
Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, says it has covered 90% of the $6.3bn (£4.7bn) assets stolen in a hack on Thursday.
The remaining 10% may take longer to source in the required amounts, the company added.
Binance has consistently pledged to cover 100% of the losses from what is suspected to be crypto's biggest hack on record and said it has set aside more than $6.34bn in company funds to do so.

articles.title_original: 'We came back from hell', say Ukrainians after years in Russia-occupied front-line city
articles.title_zh: 'We came back from hell', say Ukrainians after years in Russia-occupied front-line city
facts_zh:
'We came back from hell', say Ukrainians after years in Russia-occupied front-line city
- Published
- Warning: This story contains graphic content.
Olha has one word to describe what life has been like in the front-line city of Oleshky over the past few years: "Horror".

Disembarking alongside her from a coach in the Ukrainian region of Chernihiv with their immediate family and dog, her husband Viacheslav put it this way: "We came back from hell."
The couple were among hundreds of residents evacuated from the Russian-occupied city who crossed into northern Ukraine via Belarus on Saturday, many reuniting with loved ones they had not seen for years.

all_titles.en: 'We came back from hell', say Ukrainians after years in Russia-occupied front-line city

There were raw emotional scenes as people evacuated from the devastated Russian-occupied city of Oleshky crossed from Belarus into the Ukrainian region of Chernihiv.
Families cried as they reunited with relatives they had not seen for years, with two sisters running and crying out as they embraced their father.
Some elderly residents were so weak they were carried on stretchers.

Eight of 26 provinces are now affected, with more than 10,300 confirmed cases.
The outbreak, which started in May, became the country's deadliest in its history in August, public health officials said.

articles.title_zh: Ethiopian PM puts ministers through military training
facts_zh:
Ethiopian PM puts ministers through military training
- Published
Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has put his cabinet ministers and other senior government officials through military training, saying armed forces discipline can help build stronger leaders and advance the country's development.
Photos shared by him on social media show him taking part in military exercises alongside ministers, deputy ministers and heads of government institutions at the Hurso military training centre.
The move is unusual in Ethiopia, where senior civilian government officials are rarely seen undergoing military training.

facts_zh:
US approves sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
- Published
The United States has approved the sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine, a critically needed munition for defence against escalating Russian aerial attacks.
However, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has warned it could take "several years" for the deliveries to arrive.
The US State Department said the advanced PAC-3 interceptor missiles would cost $2.1bn (£1.6bn) and would be "funded entirely" by Kyiv's allies in Europe and Canada.

Spain train disaster clouds Sánchez chances of re-election

The breaking news from Spain this week was shocking but also shockingly familiar: another collision on the high-speed rail line south from Madrid, with reports of dozens killed.
It is just nine months since two trains crashed near Cordoba, killing 46 people.
Now 69 bodies have been recovered here in central Spain, from wreckage strewn over the tracks and down an embankment.
